name: Trip Shakespeare
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Two Harvard kids and a Minnesota bassist started a trio in Minneapolis, the city of Hüsker Dü and Prince, then added the older brother and signed to A&M. Then came Nirvana, and the label stopped knowing what to do with them.

eras.title: Wicked percussion hands
eras.text: A Harvard English major, a Harvard anthropologist and a University of Minnesota bassist land in Minneapolis, name themselves with a Star Trek pun, and press a debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare · Wikipedia: John Munson · Star Tribune: Trip Shakespeare's first two albums to be reissued Dec. 16
years.h: John Munson picks up the bass, and Trip Shakespeare has a trio
years.p: [[John Munson|54fe5175-bdf0-46b6-9732-ee8bf2fb9bcb]] joins in 1985, after Matt Wilson and Elaine Harris regroup in Minneapolis from Harvard.
years.xp:
Wilson, an English major, had posted a notice at Harvard asking for "wicked percussion hands." Harris, a graduate student in biological anthropology, answered it. Back in Minnesota they needed a bassist.

Wilson has said he hadn't first thought of Munson, remembering him as not much of a bass player. By the time Munson tried out he had improved, and Wilson says the band ended up begging him to stay.

years.p: Matt Wilson's first pick for a name mashed his two heroes, James T. Kirk and William Shakespeare.
years.xp: Dan Wilson has explained the swap: John Munson and Elaine Harris didn't want to play in a band named after Matt's two heroes, so Kirk became Trip.

years.src: Wikipedia: Applehead Man · Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare · Trouser Press: Trip Shakespeare
years.h: Applehead Man comes out on Gark, minus its percussionist
years.p: Recorded as a trio after Tim Rowe left mid-sessions to join the Nietzsches, it is the band's self-released debut.
years.xp:
It is cheerful psychedelic art-pop released into the city of [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] and [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]]. AllMusic's Timothy Monger later praised its complex harmonies. The Chicago Reader's Bill Wyman called it "an almost unlistenable excursion into overearnest art rock."

Trouser Press called it a spunky debut. It got a 1998 reissue on Clean/Twin/Tone and an expanded one from Omnivore in 2014.

eras.title: Dan comes home
eras.text: The older Wilson joins, three-part harmonies arrive, and the Gark records catch the ear of Twin/Tone and then A&M.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dan Wilson (musician) · Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare · Wikipedia: Applehead Man
years.h: Dan Wilson gets the record in the mail and joins his brother
years.p: [[Dan Wilson|9f41f18b-23b2-4052-af25-0664dbfc9085]], Matt's older brother, signs on as guitarist and pianist after hearing the debut.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports Matt sent Dan the first record almost as a demo, to lure him in. The brothers had played together at Harvard in bands called Animal Dance and the Love Monsters.

Dan studied visual arts at Harvard and graduated summa cum laude in 1983.

years.cap: Flyer for Trip Shakespeare at Off Broadway, St. Paul, Monday, Oct. 24, c. 1988
years.src: Wikipedia: Are You Shakespearienced? · Omnivore Recordings: Are You Shakespearienced? · Star Tribune: Trip Shakespeare's first two albums to be reissued Dec. 16
years.h: Are You Shakespearienced? is cut live, no headphones
years.p: Nine songs in 36 minutes, self-produced at Gark, and the first record with Dan Wilson.
years.xp:
The title winks at Jimi Hendrix. Minneapolis City Pages said "Toolmaster of Brainerd" caught the tension between Minneapolis ambition and outstate resignation.

Twin/Tone gave the Gark albums a wider release, and Omnivore's 2014 reissue says the record is what pulled A&M's attention.

years.cap: The band in a Twin/Tone label portrait
years.src: Musoscribe: A Trip Back in Time with Trip Shakespeare (Part One) · Twin/Tone Records: Trip Shakespeare · Star Tribune: Trip Shakespeare's first two albums to be reissued Dec. 16
years.p: Twin/Tone had put out the two Gark albums nationally; by 1989 a major label wanted the band too.
years.xp:
Munson dates the A&M signing to 1989, and Twin/Tone's own page dates its Trip Shakespeare catalog to the same year. Omnivore's reissue notes say the second record is what drew A&M in.

Matt Wilson later recalled that the label "really thought they could mass market Trip Shakespeare."

eras.title: Major-label money, minor-league sales
eras.text: Two records for A&M, one cut at Paisley Park and one at Pachyderm. The reviews are good and the sales aren't.

years.cap: Matt Wilson, Dan Wilson, Elaine Harris and John Munson, c. 1990
years.src: Wikipedia: Across the Universe (album) · Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare · Trouser Press: Trip Shakespeare
years.h: Across the Universe, cut at Prince's Paisley Park
years.p: Fred Maher co-produced the A&M debut, and "Snow Days" is a blues about Minnesota winters.
years.xp:
Trouser Press called it a rare case of an indie act benefiting from major-label treatment. Newsday found the jokey tone often slid into feyness.

The title tips the band's hat to the Beatles. Matt Wilson said they find themselves more in the Beatles' school than the Stones'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Across the Universe (album) · Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare
years.h: A&M's first Trip Shakespeare record sells 33,000
years.p: Matt Wilson on how Across the Universe sold, and on a record he called a compromise between what A&M wanted and what the band did.
years.xp:
Wilson described a compromise between what the label wanted on the record and what the band wanted. The 33,000 figure is cited on Wikipedia.

It is where the band's argument with A&M begins.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lulu (Trip Shakespeare album) · Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare · Fast Horse: Could the Internet Have Saved These Local Bands?
years.h: The band takes charge for Lulu, cut live at Pachyderm
years.p: Sixteen songs in 54 minutes, produced by the band and Justin Niebank. "Bachelorette" is the modern-rock single.
years.xp:
Dan Wilson has said it was the first Trip Shakespeare record where the band had nearly total creative control. Matt Wilson: "On Lulu, we finally got it right."

Sales were around 60,000, and 1991 belonged to Nirvana's Nevermind. A&M executive Wayne Isaak's reported verdict was that Trip Shakespeare was too pop to catch on as an alternative band, and the alternative scene too cliquish.

eras.title: What do we do with this?
eras.text: A&M gets a covers EP and blinks. The band is dropped and calls it.

years.cap: First Avenue's all-ages calendar lists Trip Shakespeare on Tuesday
years.h: A&M hears Volt and asks what it is supposed to do with it
years.p: A six-song covers EP gets a shrug from the label, and the band is dropped.
years.xp:
Volt covers Nick Lowe, Thunderclap Newman, Big Star, the Zombies, Hüsker Dü and Neil Young. Wikipedia says it was inspired by the 1992 Los Angeles riots and built around peace and revolution.

Munson told it this way: the label's promotions department answered the demo with "What do we do with this?" Wikipedia says the band broke up afterward. The band's own site puts its run at roughly 1986 to 1993.

eras.title: The Semisonic detour
eras.text: Dan Wilson and Munson turn into Semisonic and land a radio hit, while Matt Wilson and Munson keep a smaller thing going.

years.h: Dan Wilson and Munson start Pleasure with drummer Jacob Slichter
years.p: Matt Wilson isn't in it. By 1995 the trio is Semisonic.
years.xp: They released an EP called Pleasure on CherryDisc, then renamed themselves [[Semisonic|3037bd18-0079-4e4b-9ce1-758689e210d8]].

years.h: Semisonic's "Closing Time" climbs into the U.S. top 20
years.p: The band's album Feeling Strangely Fine makes the Trip Shakespeare alumni a hit.
years.xp: Dan Wilson told a 2008 Harvard audience that he wrote the song about the birth of his first child. It is Semisonic's biggest U.S. hit.

years.h: Matt Wilson and Munson play as the Flops
years.p: For four years they play around Minneapolis: Trip Shakespeare songs, Matt's solo songs and new ones.
years.xp: In 2003 they put out Ohh La La, a music disc plus a CD-ROM story disc with a story by Sam Magavern. By 2008 they were performing as the Twilight Hours.

years.h: Matt Wilson joins Semisonic for two sold-out First Avenue nights
years.p: December 12 and 13, with Trip Shakespeare favorites in the set.
years.xp: Matt had also added vocals and synthesizer to Semisonic's All About Chemistry. Both Trip Shakespeare and Semisonic have stars on First Avenue's exterior mural, which puts Dan Wilson and Munson in a small group with more than one.

eras.title: Back for one holiday show
eras.text: The brothers find their way back to each other, and then all four turn up on a stage they didn't book.

years.src: Musoscribe: A Trip Back in Time with Trip Shakespeare (Part One) · Wikipedia: The Flops
years.h: The Twilight Hours put out Stereo Night
years.p: Munson and Matt Wilson, the Flops under a new name, release a record.
years.xp: Munson discussed the record in a 2015 interview about the Omnivore reissues.

years.src: City Pages: Trip Shakespeare's Dan and Matt Wilson reunite for first duo show · Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare
years.h: The Wilson brothers sell out the Pantages as a duo
years.p: Dan and Matt Wilson's first shared stage since Trip Shakespeare ended almost twenty years earlier.
years.xp:
Dan told City Pages it would have been harder to think about before his own solo record Free Life had come out. Matt called the show a privilege and a little bit of a fantasy come true.

Wikipedia also lists an October 2010 benefit concert where Matt, Dan and Munson played together.

years.cap: The reunion on stage at the State Theatre, Minneapolis, December 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Trip Shakespeare · The Current: Trip Shakespeare reunite · Star Tribune: Trip Shakespeare's first two albums to be reissued Dec. 16
years.h: Elaine Harris is back, and all four play together for the first time in over twenty years
years.p: At the New Standards' holiday show they play "Susannah" and "Snow Days."
years.xp:
It was the first performance by the primary lineup in more than two decades, a short set on someone else's Christmas bill. The Current's writer caught the second night of a two-night stand at the State Theatre.

"This is the result of 20 years of pestering, mostly on my part," Munson said of the reunion.

years.src: Star Tribune: Trip Shakespeare's first two albums to be reissued Dec. 16 · Omnivore Recordings: Are You Shakespearienced?
years.h: Omnivore reissues the first two albums on colored vinyl
years.p: Applehead Man and Are You Shakespearienced? return with bonus tracks, as digipaks and as vinyl.
years.xp: Munson told the Star Tribune: "There is currently no plan. If there is great hue and cry for one we might consider it." He said the two A&M albums could get the same treatment.
